chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him):

Regarding the egg of the sandgrouse, the compensation is one sheep; if the person in ihram kills it, the compensation is like that of the ostrich egg, which is one camel. The correct interpretation of this report is to apply it to the egg in which the chick has moved, because it follows the same ruling as the ostrich egg, which indicates this.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of ihram
key_terms.بَكَارَةٌ: A young female camel (specifically one year old, used as a unit of compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing a bird egg while in ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, clarifying that the compensation (diyah) for breaking bird eggs while in ihram is contingent upon the embryo's movement, thereby distinguishing between mere existence and developed life. This biological criterion links the legal status of the egg to that of the ostrich, illustrating the Shia juristic method of deriving specific penalties from observable natural signs.
